product.title: Product Pages
product.fixSummary: Merge fix/product-page-consolidated, NOT the repair/product-* branches (their rail shipped false contents) — contents rail, 8-line Read more, eBay collapse verified on localhost; 4 notes open
product.resolution: Manual /founder-review pass, 2026-09-12. Three automatic repairs of this page (repair/product-2026-08-31-23-26-ee1b76, -09-01-12-53-izpra2, -09-01-16-16-wba960) had each re-implemented the same notes; none was merged, and none had touched real data. With the founder's go-ahead they were consolidated onto ONE branch off main, fix/product-page-consolidated (local, not pushed): 6f3a19f + 7ea3e39 cherry-picked from wba960, then 9bceec3, 22cc61a, e81b481. (1) issue-01 contents rail — the wba960 parser, audited against the live catalogue for the first time, claimed contents for 495 collected editions and many were wrong: Saga Volume 1 would have read 'Collected in this volume: #1-60' (it collects #1-6), from ComicVine's series-wide 'Collected Editions' lists merged into one run; also multi-volume blurbs, second sources, point numbering (#16.1-20.1 read as #1-20), volume/episode counts, and a mismatched enrichment (Stella Must Die described as Nightwing #16-21). 9bceec3 refuses all six shapes; 188 claims remain, every one read by hand. Verified in a real browser on localhost:3001: Descender Vol. 4 leads with 'Collected in this volume · Collects issues #17-21' (5 cards), earlier/later/all navigation expands and scrolls to #22, Back restores; Saga Vol. 1 keeps 'Issues in this series'; the one residual copied description (JMS Captain America Vol. 3) is rejected by the rail's CV-volume gate. The rail cannot confirm ranges past issue #100 (the CV issues endpoint caps at 100), so The Walking Dead Vol. 28 honestly stays in series view. Tests: 56/56 (was 33, never executed). (2) Synopsis 'too much text' — 7ea3e39 clamps to exactly 8 lines behind Read more / Show less (measured: 182px of 842px, 37 lines when open; aria-expanded + aria-controls resolve; visible focus outline; same at 390px). (3) eBay crowding — 22cc61a, with the founder's explicit OffersTable go-ahead: cheapest eBay row only, 'Show N more eBay listings' beneath it; expanded rows keep strict price order (grouping them was rejected after it listed eBay £15.99 above Travelling Man £12.99); tab counts unchanged; per-tab collapse on New/Used; keyboard Enter works. /go, AWIN, click logging untouched. Typecheck clean; lint adds nothing; test:url-filters, test:identity, test:listing-trust pass. NOT on production.
product.openFollowUp: In priority order. (A) RETAILER COVERAGE IS COLLAPSING, deadline ~2026-09-22 — this is the real cause of the 'comprehensive pricing' note, and it is feeds, not the page: listings are soft-deleted 30 days after last sighting and feeds stopped refreshing (Waterstones last seen 06-07, Wordery 05-25, WHSmith/Zavvi/AbeBooks May-June, World of Books 529,893 deleted after 08-23). Today only 2,337 products show any trusted retailer price, 16 show two, none show three. Travelling Man's remaining 2,246 live rows were last seen 08-23 and age out ~09-22; the 08-23 dry run (launch/operations/tm-revival-dryrun-latest.json, price-verify-dryrun-latest.json) already verified them safe to refresh and found 23,315 deleted TM rows still live on the site. The write run needs founder approval. (B) Synopsis MISSING: 93,243 of 136,079 listed products (68.5%) have no description and no synopsis at all; only 6.8% carry CV metadata; the enrichment checkpoint last moved 2026-08-07 (22,553 attempted, 34% match rate) — the job is not running. A free ISBN description backfill (Open Library / Google Books) is the plan-level fix; it writes canonical_products, so it needs approval. Also: many 'descriptions' are ComicVine series wiki text, not the book's blurb. (C) Creator credits: 93% of products have none stored (coverage, same cause as B). Clickable credits deliberately NOT built: /api/search for 'Brian K. Vaughan' returns zero catalogue results (lib/search has no creator matching), so a link would land on eBay-only junk. Needs a creator index/route — hands-off search SQL — plan first. The izpra2 'off-list roles' fix was measured at 0 affected products and dropped. (D) Amazon — founder manual task (10 qualifying sales), not engineering. Also seen, not touched: at 390px every product page scrolls sideways (document 644px wide) on production too — the header search form overflows; worth a mobile review.

search.title: Search
search.resolution: Both defects fixed and production-verified on 2026-08-31 (commit 7ba705a, origin/main 8cf8912). FORMAT: the search page carried its own lossy label map (ABSOLUTE/DELUXE/HARDCOVER all collapsed to "Hardcover Edition") and chose the label from detectFormat(), a TITLE heuristic, so any record without a stored format whose title said "absolute" became a hardcover. lib/identity/format.ts is now the single map used by search, product, series and volume cards: one enum value, one distinct label; an unknown format (OTHER or missing) is OMITTED, never defaulted - the product page had been calling it "Comic". Production now shows ABSOLUTE EDITION and SINGLE ISSUE side by side on /search?q=absolute+batman, zero "Hardcover Edition", and unknown-format rows show publisher only. PRICE: the cap read price.value, a field no search result has ever carried, so every row passed. It now applies to the price the card actually shows, keyed by product id rather than title, and reaches the "Other listings" and "From eBay" rails, which had rendered outside the filter entirely. Production: 52 results, Under £25 -> 19 (max £24.76), Under £15 -> 16 (max £14.96), Under £10 -> 5, Under £5 -> 0 of 52, All prices -> 52. Zero rows above threshold at any setting; count line and list agree; clearing restores. Awaiting founder re-review to move to good.

resolvedFollowUp.issue: Other listings / From eBay showed fuzzy wrong products and £0.00 stub offers
resolvedFollowUp.evidence: Root cause: unmatched listings have no product identity by definition (canonical_product_id IS NULL); the only link to the query was Postgres trigram similarity(title,q) > 0.2, and isLikelyComic() was the sole gate after it. For "absolute batman" that returned 6 rows and ZERO were the product: 3x bare "Batman" at £0.00, "Absolutely Fabulous" £6.69, "Batman vs. Two-Face (DVD)" £0.00, "Sewing for Absolute Beginners" £0.00. Nothing checked the price was real: 25,816 of 26,591 live unmatched listings (97%) are priced <= 0, and 47,302 such offers hang off 22,858 REAL products where queryA ranks offers by price ASC — so a £0.00 stub sorted first and became the "From £..." quoted to the shopper. FIX: lib/listings/trustedPrice.ts gates price >= 0.01 in SQL in queryA/queryB and in the loose-eBay mapper; lib/search/listingRelevance.ts requires every significant query word as a whole word in the title and refuses a different volume/issue number; non-book media (DVD, Blu-ray, vinyl, game, figure, calendar) added as non-comic flags. PRODUCTION VERIFIED 2026-08-31: /search?q=absolute+batman - 52 cards intact, Other listings rail now empty (all 6 rows were junk), From eBay rail all genuine Absolute Batman at £4.10-£156.70, zero £0.00 anywhere. Under £5 shows only £4.10/£4.10/£4.95/£4.10 and no £0.00 rows (it previously showed three). Second, materially different product /search?q=hellboy+omnibus: 80 cards, no £0.00, eBay rail all genuine Hellboy Omnibus £14.42-£73.50. The rail is not dead: of a 400-row sample of unmatched listings with a real price, 59 look like comics and 59/59 survive a search for their own title; "sakamoto days volume 21" returns exactly that volume at £6.29. Tests: npm run test:listing-trust, 37 assertions PASS. Format/Under-£X fix re-verified unregressed in the same pass (ABSOLUTE EDITION 23, SINGLE ISSUE 20, TRADE PAPERBACK 7, zero lossy labels).
